questions.q: Sixty four conducting drops each of radius $0 . 02m$ and each carrying a charge of $5\muC$ are combined to form a bigger drop. The ratio of surface density of bigger drop to the smaller drop will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total volume will be constant. Therefore,& $n\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}r^{3}\right) = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}R^{3} ⇒ 64\dfrac{1}{3}r = R ⇒ R = 4r$

Final surface charge density~${σ}^{'} = \dfrac{n{σ}_{0}4\pir^{2}}{4\piR^{2}} = \dfrac{64 \times {σ}_{0}r^{2}}{16r^{2}} ⇒ \dfrac{\sigma '}{\sigma0} = \dfrac{4}{1}$

questions.q: A point charge of $10 µ C$ is placed at the origin. At what location on the $X$-axis should a point charge of $40 µ C$ be placed so that the net electric field is zero at $x = 2cm$ on the $X$-axis ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the charge& $40\mu C$~be placed at a distance~${X}_{0}$~from the origin~as shown in the figure.

For the electric field at~$x = 2$~to be $0$,

${E}_{P} = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{k \times 10}{22} = \dfrac{k \times 40}{\left({X}_{0} - 2\right)2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2}{{X}_{0} - 2}$

$⇒ {X}_{0} - 2 = 4$

Therefore, the charge is located at~${X}_{0} = 4 + 2 = 6cm$

questions.q: Consider a circular loop that is uniformly charged and has a radius $\mathrm{a} \sqrt{2}$. Find the position along the positive z -axis of the cartesian coordinate system where the electric field is maximum if the ring was assumed to be placed in xy-plane at the origin :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}=\frac{\mathrm{KQr}}{\left(\mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{R}^2\right)^{3 / 2}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{dE}}{\mathrm{dx}}=0 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{2} \mathrm{a}}{\sqrt{2}}=\mathrm{a}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two identical electric point dipoles have dipole have dipole moments& $\overset{→}{p}1 = p\overset{^}{i}$~and~$\overset{→}{p}2 = - p\overset{^}{i}$~and are held on the~$x$-axis at distance '$a$'~from each other. When released, they move along the~$x$-axis with the direction of their dipole moments remaining unchanged. If the mass of each dipole is '$m$', their speed when they are infinitely far apart is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${k}_{i} + {u}_{i} = {k}_{f} + {u}_{f}$

$0 - \dfrac{2kp}{r3}{p}_{2} \cdot cos\left(180 °\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + 0$

$mv^{2} = \dfrac{2k{p}_{1}{p}_{2}}{r3}$

$⇒ \theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{2k{p}_{1}{p}_{2}}{mr^{3}}}$

${p}_{1} = {p}_{2} = p \text{ and } r = a$

$v = \dfrac{p}{a}\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2\pi{ϵ}_{0}ma}}$

questions.q: Two charges of $5Q$ and $- 2Q$ are situated at the points $( 3a, 0 )$ and $( - 5a, 0 )$ respectively. The electric flux through a sphere of radius $4a$ having centre at origin is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As can be seen from the figure above, only the $5Q$ charge is inside the spherical region.

The formula to calculate the flux through the surface is given by

$ϕ = \dfrac{qenc}{ε0} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation $( 1 )$, the flux through the given surface can be calculated as follows:

Two point charges ${q}_{1} \left(\sqrt{10}\muC\right)$and ${q}_{2} \left(-25\mu C\right)$ are placed on the $x$ -axis at $x = 1m$ and $x = 4m$ respectively. The electric field \left(\text{in}V / m\right)$ at a point $y = 3m$ on $y$-axis is,

\left[\$text{Take}\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ϵ}_{0}} =9 $\times {10}^{9}$Nm^{2}C^{- 2}\right]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electric field due to $\sqrt{10}\mu C$


${\overset{→}{E}}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{\in}_{0}}\dfrac{\sqrt{10} \times {10}^{- 6}}{{r}_{1}^{3}}{\overset{→}{r}}_{1}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4\pi{∈}_{0}}\dfrac{\sqrt{10} \times {10}^{- 6}}{ \left(\sqrt{10}\right)3} \left(- \overset{^}{i} +$3\overset{^}{j}\right)$

Similarly, electric field due to $- 25\mu C$

$\overset{→}{E}2 = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{∈}_{0}}\dfrac{25 \times {10}^{- 6}}{ \left($5\r$right)3}\left(4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j}\right)$

Net electric field,~
$\overset{→}{E} = 9 \times {10}^{9} \times {10}^{- 6}\$left(\dfrac{- \overset{^}{i}}{10} + \dfrac{3\overset{^}{j}}{10} + \dfrac{4}{5}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{3}{5}\overset{^}{j}\right)

$= 9 \times {10}^{3} \left(\dfrac{7\overset{^}{i}}{10} - \dfrac{3\overset{^}{j}}{10}\right)$

$= \left(63\overset{^}{i} - 27\overset{^}{j}\right) \times {10}^{2}\dfrac{N}{C}$

questions.q: For a uniformly charged thin spherical shell, the electric potential \left(V\right)$~radially away from the centre \left(O\right)$ of shell can be graphically represented as
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The potential is& constant inside the sphere as the electric field is zero inside the sphere. So, the value is given by&

$V = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}R}$~for~$r < R$

The potential at the surface is~

$V = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}R}$

The potential outside the sphere starts decreasing and is given by the formula~

$V = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r}$~for~$r > R$

questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{E} = - \dfrac{\overset{→}{p}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r^{3}} = - \dfrac{\overset{→}{p}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}d^{3}}$
$V = 0$

questions.q: A certain charge $Q$ is divided into two parts $q$ and~$( Q - q ) .$ How should the charges $Q$ and $q$ be divided so that $q$ and $( Q - q )$ placed at a certain distance apart experience maximum electrostatic repulsion?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${F}_{q} = \dfrac{kq ( Q - q )}{L2} = \dfrac{k}{L2} \left(qQ - q^{2}\right)$
\dfrac{\text{d}F}{\text{d}q} =$0$~when force is maximum
\dfrac{\text{d}F}{\text{d}q} = \dfrac{k}{L2} [$Q - 2q ] = 0$
$⇒ Q - 2q = 0 ⇒ Q = 2q

$

questions.q: An electron is made to enter symmetrically between two parallel and equally but oppositely charged metal plates, each of 10 cm length. The electron emerges out of the electric field region with a horizontal component of velocity $10^6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If the magnitude of the electric field between the plates is $9.1 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{cm}$, then the vertical component of velocity of electron is (mass of electron $=9.1 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$ and charge of electron $=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=\frac{\ell}{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{x}}}=\frac{10 \times 10^{-2}}{10^6}=10^{-7} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{y}}=\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{y}}+\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{y}} \mathrm{t} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{y}}=0+\frac{\mathrm{eE}}{\mathrm{m}} \times 10^{-7} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{y}}=\frac{1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31}} \times 9.1 \times 10^{-2} \times 10^{-7} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{y}}=16 \times 10^6\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I : Electric potential is constant within and at the surface of each conductor.

Statement II : Electric field just outside a charged conductor is perpendicular to the surface of the conductor at every point.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options give below.
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but and statement II is correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Statement - I: True as body of conductor acts as equipotential surface.

Statement II:& True, as conductor is equipotential. Tangential component of electric field should be zero. Therefore, electric field should be perpendicular to surface.

questions.q: In finding the electric field using Gauss law the formula \left|\overset{→}{E}\right| = \dfrac{{q}_{enc}}{{ε}_{0}\left|A\right|}$ is applicable. In the formula ${ε}_{0}$ is permittivity of free space, $A$ is the area of Gaussian surface and ${q}_{enc}$ is charge enclosed by the Gaussian surface. This equation can be used in which of the following situation?$
options: Only when the Gaussian surface is an equipotential surface
Only when the Gaussian surface is an equipotential surface and \left|\overset{→}{E}\right|$ is constant on the surface.$
Only when \left|\overset{→}{E}\right| =$ constant on the surface.$
For any choice of Gaussian surface.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Gauss law of electrostatics, the electric flux& through an enclosed surface is given by& ${ϕ}_{E} = \dfrac{qenc}{ε0}$

From the formula of electric flux,~$ϕ = \overset{→}{E} \cdot d \overset{→}{s}$

Also, the relation between electric field and electric potential is given by~$V = \overset{→}{E} \cdot d \overset{→}{r}$

So, the formula~\left|\overset{→}{E}\right| = \dfrac{qenc}{{ε}_{0}\left|A\right|}$~is only applicable~when the Gaussian surface is an equipotential surface and~\left|\overset{→}{E}\right|$& is constant on the surface.

questions.q: An electric dipole is formed by two equal and opposite charges $q$ with separation $d$ . The charges have same mass m. It is kept in a uniform electric field $E .$ If it is slightly rotated from its equilibrium orientation, then its angular frequency $\omega$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$τ = pEsin ⁡ \theta$
For small angle,
$τ = pE\theta$
$\alpha = \dfrac{τ}{I} = \dfrac{pE}{I}\theta$
\left(∵ \alpha = {\omega}^{2}\theta\right)$ Angular frequency $= \sqrt{\dfrac{pE}{I}}$
$= \sqrt{\dfrac{\left(qd\right)E}{\left(m\dfrac{d^{2}}{4} + m\dfrac{d^{2}}{4}\right)}}$
$= \sqrt{\dfrac{2qE}{md}}$

$

It is brought near to an infinitely long nonconducting sheet of charge density ' $\sigma$ ' as shown in figure. If string subtends an angle of $45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ with the sheet at equilibrium the charge density of sheet will be :
(Given, $\varepsilon_0=8.85 \times 10^{-12} \frac{\mathrm{~F}}{\mathrm{~m}}$ and acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$)

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{qE}=\mathrm{mg} \\ & \mathrm{q}\left[\frac{\sigma}{2 \varepsilon_0}\right]=\mathrm{mg} \\ & \sigma=\frac{2 \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{q}} \\ & \sigma=\frac{2 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 100 \times 10^{-6} \times 10}{10 \times 10^{-6}} \\ & \sigma=17.7 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^2 \\ & \sigma=1.77 \mathrm{nC} / \mathrm{m}^2\end{aligned}$

(b) A charge $q$& is placed at the centre of a cube. The flux through all the faces will be the same.

questions.subject: Physics

We know that electric flux is a scalar quantity and this is the scalar product of the magnitude of electric field and surface area.&

Recall, the formula given by Gauss theorem,& $ϕ = \overset{→}{E} \cdot \overset{→}{A} = EAcos\theta$, here~$\theta = 90 °$, it means,~$ϕ = 0$.

questions.q: If the electric potential at any point \left(x, y, z\right)m$ in space is given by $V = 3x^{2}$ volt. The electric field at the point \left(1, 0, 3\right)m$ will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electric potential& $V = 3x^{2}$

Electric potential and electric field are related as~$E = - \dfrac{d V}{d x} = - 6x$.

At the point~\left(1, 0, 3\right)m$,~

$⇒ E = - 6 \times 1 = - 6Vm^{- 1}$

Thus, electric field is~$6Vm^{- 1}$~along negative $x ‐$ axis.

$

questions.q: ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ are two hollow concentric cubes enclosing charges $2Q$ and $3Q$ respectively as shown in figure. The ratio of electric flux passing through ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Gauss's law states that the net flux of an electric field in a closed surface is directly proportional to the enclosed electric charge. Therefore,

${ϕ}_{smaller cube} = \dfrac{2Q}{ε0}$

Since the smaller cube is inside the bigger cube, so total charge contained by the bigger cube will be $2Q + 3Q = 5Q$.

${ϕ}_{bigger cube} = \dfrac{5Q}{ε0}$

Therefore, required ratio will be,

$\dfrac{ϕ\text{smaller cube}}{ϕ\text{bigger cube}} = \dfrac{2}{5}$.

questions.q: Three point charges $q, - 2q$ and $2q$ are placed on $x$ axis at a distance $x = 0, x = \dfrac{3}{4}R$ and $x = R$ respectively from origin as shown. If $q = 2 \times {10}^{- 6}C$ and $R = 2cm$, the magnitude of net force experienced by the charge $- 2q$ is~_____ $N$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The net force on the given charge will be the resultant of the forces due to the other two charges.

Hence, the net force& \left({F}_{n}\right)$~can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}{F}_{n} & = & \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{4q^{2}}{\left(\dfrac{R}{4}\right)2} - \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{2q^{2}}{\left(\dfrac{3R}{4}\right)2} \\ & = & 9 \times {10}^{9} \times \dfrac{16q^{2}}{R2}\left[4 - \dfrac{2}{9}\right] \\ & = & 9 \times {10}^{9} \times \dfrac{16 \times \left(2 \times {10}^{- 6}C\right)2}{\left(0 . 02m\right)2} \times \dfrac{34}{9} \\ & = & 5440N\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: Two electric dipoles of dipole moments $1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 30}cm$ and $2 . 4 \times {10}^{- 30}cm$ are placed in two difference uniform electric fields of strengths $5 \times {10}^{4}NC^{- 1}$ and $15 \times {10}^{4}NC^{- 1}$ respectively. The ratio of maximum torque experienced by the electric dipoles will be $\dfrac{1}{x}$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum torque experienced by an electric dipole is& ${τ}_\max = PEsin90 °$.

So,~\left|τ\right|max = PE$

The ratio is~$\dfrac{τ1}{τ2} = \dfrac{{P}_{1}{E}_{1}}{{P}_{2}{E}_{2}} = \dfrac{1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 30} \times 5 \times {10}^{4}}{2 \cdot 4 \times {10}^{- 30} \times 15 \times {10}^{4}} = \dfrac{1}{6}$
~

Hence, the value of~$x = 6$.

$

questions.q: The electric field in a region is given by $\overset{→}{E} = \left(\dfrac{3}{5}{E}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4}{5}{E}_{0}\overset{^}{j}\right)NC^{- 1}$. The ratio of flux of reported field through the rectangular surface of area $0 . 2m^{2}$ (parallel to $y - z$~plane) to that of the surface of area $0 . 3m^{2}$ (parallel to $x - z$ plane) is $a: b = a: 2,$~where $a = ?$~[Here $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{^}{k}$ are unit vectors along $x, y$ and $z$ -axes respectively]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{E} = \left(\dfrac{3{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{j}\right)NC^{- 1}$

${A}_{1} = 0 . 2m^{2}$ [parallel to $y - z$ plane]

$= \overset{→}{A}1 = 0 . 2m^{2}\overset{^}{i}$

${A}_{2} = 0 . 3m^{2}$ [parallel to $x - z$ plane]

$\overset{→}{A}2 = 0 . 3m^{2}\overset{^}{j}$

Now,~${ϕ}_{a} = \left[\dfrac{3{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{j}\right] \cdot \left[0 . 2\overset{^}{i}\right] = \dfrac{3 \times 0 . 2}{5}{E}_{0}$

$ \text{ and } {ϕ}_{b} = \left[\dfrac{3{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{j}\right] \cdot \left[0 . 3\overset{^}{j}\right] = \dfrac{4 \times 0 . 3}{5}{E}_{0}$

Now,~$\dfrac{ϕa}{ϕb} = \dfrac{0 . 6}{1 . 2} = \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{a}{b}$

$⇒ a: b = 1: 2$

$⇒ a = 1$

questions.q: An electron is released from rest near an infinite non-conducting sheet of uniform charge density ' $-\sigma$ '. The rate of change of de-Broglie wave length associated with the electron varies inversely as $\mathrmn^{\text {th }}$ power of time. The numerical value of $n$ is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the momentum of $\mathrme^{-}$at any time t is p and its de-broglie wavelength is $\lambda$.
Then, $\mathrm{p}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\lambda}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{dp}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{-\mathrm{h}}{\lambda^2} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ & \mathrm{ma}=\mathrm{F}=-\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\lambda} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \quad[\mathrm{~m}=\text { mass of } \mathrm{e}]
\end{aligned}$
Where, -ve sign represents decrease in $\lambda$ with time
$\mathrm{ma}=\frac{-\mathrm{h}}{(\mathrm{~h} / \mathrm{p})^2} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{a}=-\frac{\mathrm{p}^2}{\mathrm{mh}} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ & \mathrm{a}=-\frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{\mathrm{~h}} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\frac{\mathrm{ah}}{\mathrm{mv}^2}...(1)
\end{aligned}$
here, $\mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{qE}}{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}} \frac{\sigma}{2 \varepsilon_0}$
$\mathrm{a}=\frac{\sigma \mathrm{e}}{2 \mathrm{~m} \varepsilon_0}$
and $\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{u}+\mathrm{at}$
$\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{at}$
Substituting values of a \& v in equation (1)
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\frac{2 \mathrm{~h} \varepsilon_0}{\sigma \mathrm{et}^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=2
\end{aligned}$
